quests.title: The Exile: Blooming

dialogue.t: If it weren't for you, I don't think I'd have ever seen these roses sprout.
If only I knew this would happen... instead of seeds, I should have brought a few more books.
Are you surprised? Well, I guess that means that I've adapted pretty well.
When I first got here, I was unable to get used to anything, whether it be the food, the housing, or anything else.
But I got used to everything over time.
That doesn't mean that I've fully accepted my predicament, though.
I suppose it is impossible to make roses from Sumeru City bloom here after all.
I could have been called that once, but not anymore.
I said something beyond my station, and learned something I shouldn't have.
I broke the Akademiya's taboos, so I was removed from amongst their ranks.
Curiosity is the impetus for seeking wisdom, but it's also the cause of sin.
I only understood that after I was exiled to this place.
For safety reasons, I don't think I should go into details.
Ahem, but...
I thought adventurers would just come and go, never coming back to chit-chat after finishing their jobs.
I didn't expect to have another long conversation with you.
To be honest, I don't have a lot of friends to talk to here.
Do you think... at some point... you would be able to come by and fertilize my plants again?
...Okay then, I'll wait for you.
There you are. You're very punctual.
I made some Butter Chicken. You're welcome to dine with me if you're hungry.
Butter Chicken! How could we refuse? A big plate for Paimon, please!
Okay, sorry...
It's okay, there's no need to be so formal. It's only human nature to love food.
I'll heat some up and pack it for you. It's the least I could do to show my gratitude for your help.
You're so nice, Miss Sabbah! Your roses will surely grow and flower, just like you wanted!
Well, I've been keeping the soil moist, so the sprouts have been coming along.
My only worry is that they are growing slowly.
Generally speaking, if a germ is in good shape, it should grow quickly enough, but these few have been dormant so far...
I'm not sure if it's because the soil isn't fertile enough. I may have to add more fertilizer if this keeps up.

dialogue.sit: We can try using Dendro again.

dialogue.t: Would you do me this favor, then?
Piece of cake. We got this!
You don't seem to have a Vision, and yet you can control Dendro. You're no ordinary adventurer, I think.
Supposedly, there are people who can control the elements without a Vision, but such people are of universally ill repute...
You, however, have a good heart. Don't stray onto the wrong path!
Thank you again. Honestly, it gladdens my heart to see Sumeru Roses grow in this environment.

dialogue.sit: As you talk to Sabbah, new leaves begin to sprout...
The leaves unfold, revealing flower buds.
The flower buds slowly open and blossom into Sumeru Roses.
Sabbah picks one and hands it to you and Paimon.

dialogue.t: You shouldn't have... You didn't have many to begin with...
It's all right. After all, this wouldn't have been possible without your help.

dialogue.sit: We were just lending a hand.

dialogue.t: A rose garden is magnificent, but a single rose also has beauty of its own. I've been intrigued by roses ever since my scholarly days.
What? You were a researcher?
Right, I haven't told you yet... I'm not a native of Aaru Village. I "moved" here from the Akademiya.
See, didn't Paimon tell you that Miss Sabbah speaks in a refined way, just like the researchers we've met?
You planted these because you wanted to continue studying roses, right?
I wouldn't say that. To be honest, I don't think that researchers' interest in their subjects should be cultivated just for research's sake alone.
I did this because I love this world and want to understand the life cycle of plants.
As for me, I once studied the impact of geographical changes on the evolution of roses.
Just consider this. If the environments in Sumeru had changed in a totally different way, how would these roses have adapted?
Would they have crawled up the walls like ivy? If so, the walls of the Akademiya would now be covered in roses.
Would they have formed clusters? A natural bouquet! Wouldn't that have been lovely?
Maybe they might have even developed a spectrum of colors... White, red, and gold... Brand new species in their own right.
Of course, very few people discover new species nowadays, much less develop new species like the top researchers used to do.
What I want to say is that there's a vast amount of potential in every rose.
Exploring the possibilities is a lot of fun for me. Back then, I would happily collect samples every day.
Looking back now, that was a simple and joyful time.
Anyway, just take it. To me, this is no loss. I am freely sharing my happiness.
If you still feel awkward, just visit me often, and bring some Sumeru Roses with you.
I feel at ease when I talk to you.
And no matter what I said, you never thought it was nonsense or interrupted me.
I'll have small gifts for you too. Though I have no use for them now, you might like them.
Please do return.

quests.description: A rose that once bloomed in Sumeru City may be able to bloom elsewhere, too.
